findings.domain: Cloud & Data Architecture / Cloud Landing Zone & Tenancy
findings.issue: The design does not encrypt on-premises connectivity, violating [cloud-data-protection-standard.md §3.2].
findings.recommendation: Implement IPsec overlay for on-premises connectivity.
findings.evidence_excerpt: On-premises connectivity uses two 10 Gbps Direct Connect connections from the Dublin and Frankfurt data centres, without an IPsec overlay, to avoid the throughput limit of VPN tunnels.

findings.domain: Cloud & Data Architecture / Cloud Landing Zone & Tenancy
findings.issue: The design does not enforce inspection of spoke-to-spoke traffic, violating [cloud-landing-zone-standard.md §5.1].
findings.recommendation: Implement a centralised inspection VPC and configure spoke VPCs to route traffic through it.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Each workload VPC has a single default route, 0.0.0.0/0, pointing to its Transit Gateway attachment.

findings.domain: Cloud & Data Architecture / Cloud Network Controls
findings.issue: The design allows spoke-to-spoke traffic to bypass inspection, violating [cloud-landing-zone-standard.md §5.1] Network topology.
findings.recommendation: Implement inspection for spoke-to-spoke traffic, either by routing through the inspection VPC or using a different architecture.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The central web ACLs run the AWS managed rule groups in count mode, and application teams can ask for blocking mode once they have finished tuning false positives.

findings.domain: Cloud & Data Architecture / Data Protection & Storage
findings.issue: The datalake-etl role has read and write access to all zones, violating the requirement for least-privilege policies scoped to specific actions and resource identifiers.
findings.recommendation: Revoke the datalake-etl role's access to all zones and re-grant it only the necessary permissions for each zone.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Ingestion jobs in workload accounts deliver data by assuming the datalake-etl role, which has read and write access to all zones.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Cryptography & Key Management
findings.issue: The design does not describe a defined cryptoperiod for key classes, which is required by [cryptography-key-management-standard.md §5.2].
findings.recommendation: Define a cryptoperiod for key classes and ensure rotation mechanisms are in place.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Both Direct Connect connections use MACsec encryption at layer 2, with the connectivity association keys stored in AWS Secrets Manager in the network account.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Cryptography & Key Management
findings.issue: The design does not describe a key recovery or escrow procedure, which is required by [cryptography-key-management-standard.md §5.2].
findings.recommendation: Implement a key recovery or escrow procedure.
findings.evidence_excerpt: All data lake buckets use SSE-KMS with these keys, and S3 Block Public Access is enforced at account level in every account.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Identity & Privileged Access
findings.issue: Break-glass access does not use phishing-resistant MFA, violating [identity-access-standard.md §2.1] Multi-factor authentication Requirement: Administrative and privileged access MUST use phishing-resistant factors — FIDO2 security keys, platform passkeys, or certificate-based authentication.
findings.recommendation: Enable phishing-resistant MFA for break-glass users, e.g. using FIDO2 security keys or platform passkeys.
findings.evidence_excerpt: MFA is not enabled on the break-glass users, so that access does not depend on a hardware token being available during an incident.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Identity & Privileged Access
findings.issue: Administrators connect to production from general-purpose workstations.
findings.recommendation: Broker administrative sessions through a privileged access management solution with session recording, or originate from a dedicated privileged access workstation.
findings.evidence_excerpt: The hlm-security-tooling account is the delegated administrator for GuardDuty, Security Hub, IAM Access Analyzer, Amazon Macie and the AWS Config aggregator.

findings.issue: The SCP DenyAll does not terminate in an explicit deny-all rule with logging enabled, violating segmentation-standard.md §4.2.
findings.recommendation: Replace DenyAll with an explicit deny-all rule with logging enabled.

findings.domain: Cloud & Data Architecture / Data Protection & Storage
findings.issue: The log buckets use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, but the retention period is not tied to a business or regulatory requirement, violating [cloud-data-protection-standard.md §4.1].
findings.recommendation: Define a retention period tied to a business or regulatory requirement and automate disposal at the end of it.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Log buckets use SSE-KMS and S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a retention period of one year, after which objects move to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for a further six years.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Identity & Privileged Access
findings.issue: The design relies on FIDO2 security-key MFA for privileged access, but does not explicitly state that administrative access also uses MFA.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly state that administrative access also uses FIDO2 security-key MFA.
findings.evidence_excerpt: All human access goes through IAM Identity Center federated with the corporate IdP, which enforces FIDO2 security-key MFA on every sign-in to the AWS application.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Identity & Privileged Access
findings.issue: Permissions are assigned to groups rather than individual users.
findings.recommendation: Consider assigning permissions to individual users instead of groups.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Permission sets are assigned to IdP groups, never to individual users.

findings.domain: Cyber / Security Architecture / Identity & Privileged Access
findings.issue: Break-glass access credentials are stored in a shared vault folder accessible by 25 team members, violating [identity-access-standard.md §6.1] Break-glass Requirement: Break-glass accounts MUST have vaulted credentials split under dual control.
findings.recommendation: Split break-glass access credentials under dual control, e.g. using AWS IAM password policy to require two approvers for password changes.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Their passwords are stored in the infrastructure team's shared vault folder, which all 25 members of the infrastructure team can open.

findings.issue: No dependency, container or supply-chain scanning is described in the pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Add SCA and container image scanning as blocking pipeline gates, publish an SBOM per release, and fail the build on new critical CVEs in direct dependencies.

findings.issue: The design does not state where its trust boundaries lie. Controls are only meaningful relative to a boundary, so authentication placement, filtering and encryption requirements cannot be judged.
findings.recommendation: Mark the trust boundaries on the architecture diagram and state, for each boundary crossing, what authenticates and what is filtered.

findings.issue: No threat model or documented attack-surface analysis accompanies the design.
findings.recommendation: Produce a STRIDE or equivalent threat model covering every trust boundary in the design, with mitigations traced to specific controls and residual risks accepted by a named owner.
